promptState.text: Make a modern premium coffee ad from the first picture. Keep the mug exactly as it is, standing on a round dark stone podium in the middle. A dark charcoal background that fills the whole picture from edge to edge, with a soft blurred orange glow behind the mug, warm orange rim light along the edges of the mug, and a few roasted coffee beans on the podium. Put the logo from the second picture small and white at the top. Below the logo, the big bold white headline "START YOUR DAY BOLD" in one clean modern sans-serif font. Under the podium, a rounded orange button with the white words "ORDER NOW". No other text.

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Ming Image 0.1 Design) - The image model itself, 6B, from inclusionAI (Ant Group). It is made for design: posters, flyers, ads, UI screens, infographics, anything with text.
  • Load CLIP (Ling mini 2.0) - Reads your prompt and looks at both pictures.
  • Load VAE - Turns the finished render into a picture. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can make transparent pictures.

 The speed node

Teal, above the graph.

  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. The Run Times note has the numbers. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load Image - Product - The product photo the ad is made from. The result keeps its shape.
  • 2. Load Image - Logo - Your logo. It can be any shape: the helpers below shrink it into a strip at the top of a white picture the size of the result, so Ming puts it small at the top of the ad.
  • 3. Output Size - How many pixels the result has. Pick a line from the list: 1024 is about 1 megapixel and fast, 2048 is Ming's 2K and slower. This workflow opens at 1024. Your picture keeps its shape either way.
  • 4. Add a prompt - What to make, and what to keep. Call the pictures the first picture and the second picture. Put every word you want written in quotes.
  • 5. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same result, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves.

  • Scale Image to Total Pixels - Works out the exact size at the Output Size you picked: that many pixels, in steps of 32, in your picture's shape. Only that size is used.
  • Get Image Size - Reads that size as a width and a height for the nodes that need it.
  • Resize Crop Pixaroma - Scales your picture to that size and crops the few pixels that do not fit, so nothing is stretched and the result lines up with your picture in the Compare.
  • Math Expression - Works out a fifth of the result's height, a // 5, for the logo strip.
  • Resize And Pad Image - Fits the logo into that strip, as wide as the result, centred, with white around it, so it is never stretched.
  • Empty Image - A white picture the size of the result.
  • Image Composite Masked - Puts the logo strip at the top of the white picture. That is the second picture Ming sees. Ming copies a second picture where things sit in it: when the logo was padded into the middle instead, a Run drew a huge black copy of it right over the mug. With the logo at the top, it stayed small at the top on 28 of 28 test runs.
  • ModelSamplingFlux - Tunes the model to the size of the result. 1.15 and 0.5 are the settings from ComfyUI's own template.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Ming Image Edit - Reads your prompt and both pictures. It has room for up to 8; this workflow uses two.
  • ConditioningZeroOut - An empty negative prompt. This model is made for CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler needs one plugged in.
  • Empty Latent Image - The blank canvas for the result, at the size from the helpers.
  • KSampler - The render: 12 steps, lcm, simple, CFG 1. ComfyUI's own template uses a chain of custom sampler nodes with a tuned lcm sampler; the plain KSampler gave results of the same quality and the same layout in 10 test pairs, so the simpler one stays.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Image Compare Pixaroma - The product picture and the result, one over the other. Move the mouse across it to slide between them.
  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the result and saves it to your output folder as a PNG.

The dark Run Timer above them shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

SETTINGS

 What this workflow makes

An ad from two pictures, with Ming Image 0.1 Design: here, a plain photo of a black mug and the Pixaroma logo become a modern coffee ad. The mug stands on a dark stone podium with a soft orange glow behind it, orange light along its edges and a few coffee beans, with the logo at the top, the headline START YOUR DAY BOLD and an orange ORDER NOW button.

How it got there, with the same two pictures:

TriedResult
The first demo: the mug on a flat warm orange backgroundEvery word right, but a flat, plain look
Dark charcoal, orange glow, a podium, coffee beans, a buttonWords right on 4 of 4, but white bars at the sides on 1
The same, with the background filling the whole picture from edge to edgeNo bars on 8 of 8
The logo padded into the middle of the second pictureOn one Run, a huge black copy of the logo right over the mug
The logo placed small at the top of the second picture, this workflowLogo at the top on 16 of 16 at 1536, that seed included, and 8 of 8 at 1024. Headline right on 8 of 8 at 1024 and 14 of 16 at 1536

If a letter of the headline comes out wrong, Run again with a new seed. Three other looks were tried on 4 seeds each and worked less well: a coffee splash around the mug (the splash covered the mug on 2), the mug on a cafe table by a window (the headline was misspelled on 2) and a split layout with the words on a dark half (the mug turned brown on 2). A tall guitar photo with "PLAY IT LOUD" kept the logo at the top on 4 of 4, but one dropped the word IT.

 Writing the prompt

  • Call the pictures the first picture and the second picture. Naming them image 1, <image1> or by what is in them gave the same results.
  • Say what to keep: the demo says keep the mug exactly as it is.
  • A modern look comes from the light and the setting: a dark background with a soft orange glow, light along the edges of the product, and something for it to stand on. The flat coloured background of the first demo looked plain.
  • Say a dark charcoal background that fills the whole picture from edge to edge, or the background can stop short and leave white bars at the sides.
  • Put every word you want written in quotes, say where it goes, and end with No other text.. Without it, Ming added garbled small print along the bottom on some seeds.

Not reliable: printing a logo onto a product. Asked to put the logo on a light guitar, Ming laid a huge black copy of the logo over the whole picture in 15 of 28 tests, whatever the wording. It tends to copy the second picture where it sits in its own frame, which is also why a logo on a black mug came out much bigger than asked. This workflow uses that copying on purpose: the helpers put the logo small at the top of the second picture, so that is where it lands in the ad.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Settings","icon":"gear","color":"#2a9d8f"}}

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 How long a Run takes

Output SizeResultNew picture or promptNew seed only
1024 - about 1 MP1024 x 102413.5 s9.2 s
1536 - about 2.4 MP1536 x 153629 to 38 s25 s
2048 - about 4 MP, 2K2048 x 204864 s57 s

The result sizes are for a square product photo like the demo one. Two pictures make every step slower than editing one. Change a picture or the prompt and the text encoder reads them again, which is the first time column; change only the seed and it reuses what it read.

This workflow opens at 1024: with the logo placed at the top of the second picture, 1024 had the logo and the headline right on 8 of 8. Pick 1536 or 2048 for a sharper ad once you like the prompt.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the attention maths. On the same seed at Output Size 2048, it took 30 s, against 55 s with the normal pytorch attention. The result was a different variation, not a worse one. In a test that had to keep a portrait exactly as it was, normal attention kept slightly more of it unchanged on 3 of 4 seeds, so switch to pytorch attention when the edit must touch as little as possible. To compare it yourself, switch the node to pytorch attention.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI has to load 5.75 GB of image model and 18.2 GB of text encoder. Measured on the demo at 1024 with the models unloaded first: 17 s, against 13.5 s once they were loaded.

That was with the model files still in this machine's file cache. The very first load after switching the computer on reads them off the disk for real and will be slower; that case was not measured, so no number is given for it.

 Smaller graphics cards

ComfyUI loads this model in pieces, so it does not have to fit on the card in one go. In a test of the one-picture Image Edit workflow, an edit went past a limit of about 8 GB, to about 11.5 GB, because reading a picture takes extra working memory. This workflow reads two pictures, so expect more; it was not measured with two. With nothing limiting it, it took about 23 GB of this 24 GB card: ComfyUI uses the room it has.

That test ran on a 4090, so it shows what fits, not how fast a smaller card is. A slower card takes longer, and Output Size 2048 takes five to six times as long as 1024 here, and 1536 two to three times. On a slower card, try prompts at 1024 first.

 System RAM

With the whole card to itself, ComfyUI held 6 to 9 GB of RAM in the one-picture Image Edit workflow. The smaller the card, the more of the models wait in RAM instead: up to about 22 GB when it was told to use 6 GB of the card. Plan on 32 GB of RAM at the very least. A smaller version of the text encoder (w4a8, 12.8 GB) is in the More versions list; it was not tested here.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
